episodes.212543: Isolated thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall during the late afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.212554: Slow-moving thunderstorms over Central Alabama dumped heavy rainfall in short periods of time during the afternoon and evening hours of June 7. Flash flooding issues developed in the Gadsden and Birmingham areas as 1-3 inches of rain fell quickly, with numerous flooding reports from urban or low-lying roadways. In addition, numerous trees and several power lines were downed around Gadsden and Attalla, caused by sub-severe winds aided by heavy rain and water-logged soils.
episodes.212561: A low pressure system moved through the region and spread thunderstorms across far eastern Montana, a few of which became severe.
episodes.212563: Mid level moisture pulled up ahead of an upper level disturbance over the western U.S. combined with intense daytime heating resulted in the development of high based showers and thunderstorms across west central New Mexico midday June 8th moving northeast across central New Mexico during the late afternoon and early evening hours. Little to no rainfall from these high based showers and thunderstorms reached the ground and instead resulted in erratic wind gusts and areas of blowing dust. Some of these virga showers and dry thunderstorms resulted in severe wind gusts at a personal weather station in western Albuquerque and at the Santa Fe Municipal Airport. The disturbance moved across the state on June 9th resulting in high based showers and storms across central New Mexico and wetter strong to severe storms across eastern New Mexico due to higher low level moisture across this part of the state. Severe wind gusts were observed at the Wild Rivers RAWS near Questa and at Conchas Lake State Park. Finally, very dry and gusty winds were observed across far western New Mexico with a brief high wind gust at Gallup Municipal Airport during the afternoon hours June 9th.
episodes.212740: Supercell thunderstorms rolled across the Denver Metro area mid afternoon on June 8th producing up to golf ball sized hail. Isolate severe wind gusts were recorded as well. As the storms progressed east of the Denver their intensity increase. A supercell thunderstorm continued to track eastward, stay south of I-70. Farther north, thunderstorms organized into a broken line, producing wind gusts of 55 to 70 mph across far northeast Colorado.
episodes.212753: A line of storms moving across north central and northeast South Dakota generated high winds from the evening of June 7th into the early morning hours of June 8th. The South Dakota State University mesonet station 1 mile southwest of Timber Lake recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph, while the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet stations 1 mile northeast of Timber Lake and 2 miles north of Herreid peaked at 64 mph.
episodes.212876: Warmer and much drier conditions emerged on the afternoon of the seventh. However, one isolated thunderstorm was able to develop over eastern Hockley County. This thunderstorm was short lived but produced severe winds as it collapsed. An NWS storm survey was conducted which revealed damage to a couple of buildings in eastern Hockley County north of Ropesville.
episodes.212880: Rich moisture advected into the region ahead of a dryline positioned across the south-central Texas Panhandle into the southwestern South Plains. Strong heating ahead of the dryline and a weak short wave trough aloft allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop across the central South Plains. A well mixed boundary layer allowed for storms to be high based and produce strong wind gusts. One Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Abernathy (Hale County) recorded severe wind gusts with the outflow well ahead of the parent thunderstorm. Weak flow allowed for storms to have little to no movement which produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding in Hockley County.
episodes.213070: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of June 8th.
episodes.213127: During the morning of June 7th, training thunderstorms caused flooding across nearly the entire southern half of Boone County. Most of the flooding consisted of inches of water over roadways and flooded creeks. That afternoon through evening, additional thunderstorms exacerbated the problem, creating even more dangerous conditions through the morning of the 8th.
episodes.213129: During the afternoon and early evening hours of June 8th, multi-cell clusters moved over portions of west-central and south-central Illinois. These resulted in minor flooding and isolated wind damage.
episodes.213164: Severe thunderstorms swept through the Missouri Ozarks during the evening and overnight hours of June 7th and 8th. Several tornadoes occurred along with significant flash flooding. Between 2 and 6 inches of rainfall fell over a short period of time across portions of southwest Missouri.
episodes.213166: Significant flash flooding occurred during the morning of June 8th. Between 2 and 6 inches of rainfall fell over a short period of time in southeast Kansas.
episodes.213384: A backdoor cold front interacting with a moist and unstable air mass resulted in a nearly stationary area of showers and thunderstorms in west central Davidson County during the evening hours. As much as one to three inches of rain fell in a short period of time, resulting in a report of flash flooding in Lexington.
episodes.213637: A cold front pushed south across the area resulting in widely scattered severe thunderstorms over western Nebraska during the evening and late evening hours. Mostly strong gusty winds were reported along with small hail. A landspout tornado was also reported earlier in the afternoon.
episodes.213644: A long duration severe weather event began across southeast Wyoming during the early afternoon of June 8th and continued into the late evening hours across western Nebraska. Many strong wind gusts over 60 MPH were reported, along with large hail, flash flooding, and a tornado.
episodes.213753: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.213978: Thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 8th. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind and hail up to penny size. Locally heavy rainfall resulted in some flash flooding.
episodes.213979: Thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the morning hours of the 8th. Locally heavy rainfall from this activity resulted in some flash flooding across portions of Benton and Washington Counties.
episodes.214065: An anomalously wet air mass was in place across East Tennessee on Monday June 8, 2026. An upper level shortwave lifting north from the Ozarks into the Upper Midwest during the day, lead to widespread shower and thunderstorm activity across the forecast area, resulting in some flash flooding primarily in the Knoxville metro area.
episodes.214591: An upper level low and surface cold front combined with a very unstable airmass resulted in severe thunderstorms across western and central North Dakota. Supercell thunderstorms initially produced very large hail before transitioning to a linear storm mode, which led to widespread significant thunderstorm wind gusts. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, occurring southwest of Medora in Billings County. Measured wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common as storms moved across western and central North Dakota. The area with the most significant wind damage occurred across Stark, Morton, Mercer, and McLean Counties. In a swath from Dickinson, to Hebron, to Beulah, to Douglas Bay, to west of Garrison, damage from thunderstorm wind gusts led to winds estimated from 80 to 100 mph. The strongest measured wind gust came from a personal weather station just east of Beulah that reported a gust of 103 mph. Damage included campers turned over, large trees downed, roof damage, power outages, garages destroyed, vehicle damage, siding damage, and dented grain bins.
episodes.214838: An upper-level disturbance interacting with a surface trough triggered clusters of showers and thunderstorms across central Illinois from the late morning through the afternoon of June 8th.  With surface dewpoints in the lower to middle 70s and copious moisture within the atmospheric profile, the storms were efficient rain-producers.  There were pockets of rainfall of 1.50 to 3.00, with a few spots exceeding 4.00.  The most widespread heavy rainfall and flash flooding was focused along the I-57 corridor from Douglas County southward to Effingham County.
episodes.214850: A large thunderstorm complex moved across western and central ND during the evening hours of June 7th. As it moved into to the western part of the Devils Lake Basin a severe wind gust of 59 mph was measured before the complex weakened becoming sub-severe.
episodes.214959: Thunderstorms developed over the western Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of July 7th. As this activity pushed east, it became severe. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported in the Antioch area of southern Sheridan County. Thunderstorms weakened as they moved east of the panhandle into the northwestern Sandhills during the late evening hours.
episodes.215006: More organized thunderstorms developed and a few supecell storms managed to get going across northwestern SD. These supercells were responsible for large hail (+2) and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215066: Severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds to eastern Wyoming.
episodes.215103: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon along a stationary front. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Caldwell County.
episodes.215151: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a sharp dryline from the late afternoon through the late evening hours on the 8th across portions of east-central and northeast Colorado. Storm motions were mostly to the east. Up to four inch diameter hail occurred in Kit Carson county, and winds up to 69 mph occurred in Yuma county.
episodes.215242: A cold front moved across western and central Wyoming and brought a scattering of showers and thunderstorms. With large dew point depressions and supportive upper level dynamics, strong wind gusts occurred across much of central Wyoming. The most widespread high wind gusts were in Johnson County. After the cold front passage, a brief period of high wind driven by a tight pressure gradient and northwest flow brought strong synoptic winds to Johnson County.
episodes.215661: A cluster of thunderstorms slowly moved and trained over the same areas of southeast Kansas during the early morning hours of June 8th. The heavy rainfall resulted in flash-flooding across Neosho and Labette counties.
episodes.216099: Multiple severe storms occurred, producing winds up to 67 mph and hail up to 3 inches in diameter. Some minor flooding occurred as well.

A combination of NWS ground surveys and Sentinel-2 satellite analysis concluded that an EF1 tornado began within a forested area in far western Douglas County and tracked 8.9 miles, passing by Arden, and ending southeast of Tigris. Along the track, the tornado produced an intermittent path of extensive tree damage and caused roof damage to a couple outbuildings and pushed a manufactured home several feet. The tornado peaked with estimated winds of 100 mph and was 400 yards at its widest point.

Based on the damage done this tornado was rated EF-1, and from that wind speeds were estimated to be around 95 mph.
